backlog.title: Align Implementation to PRD Spec — Selection + Dwell Relevance Model
backlog.description: The PRD (PRD.md) is a reference spec describing the desired final state of the tmux-session-history engine. The current implementation has diverged: it ships a client_activity-polling activity-detection subsystem that the PRD explicitly removes (PRD §12: 'It is therefore not wired. Relevance comes from selection and dwell only.'). This phase is a simplification refactor: strip the activity-detection machinery (do_activity, do_poller, do_start_poller, the activity/poller subcommands, @session-history-poller-pid, @session-history-piped-pane), raise the dwell default from 10000 ms to 30000 ms (the coupled compensating change — once focused-activity is gone, dwell becomes the only silent-presence signal), and update all code comments and user-facing documentation to match. The reactive engine core (do_hook, do_dwell, do_toggle, do_back/forward, do_pick, prune_dead, cap_to_live) is already PRD-compliant and must NOT be modified. See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/system_context.md for the full context.

tasks.title: Remove Activity Detection Functions & Subcommands
tasks.description: Delete the three activity-detection functions (do_activity, do_poller, do_start_poller) and remove their case-dispatch branches and Usage-string tokens so the subcommand set matches PRD §17 exactly.

subtasks.title: Delete do_activity(), do_poller(), and do_start_poller() functions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/gap_analysis.md GAP 1. The current engine (scripts/session_history.sh) implements a client_activity-polling activity promoter as a THIRD relevance path. PRD §12 explicitly states: 'It is therefore not wired. Relevance comes from selection and dwell only.' PRD §6 lists exactly two promotion causes: (1) direct selection, (2) dwell. The functions to delete are: do_activity() (~lines 320-341 incl. divider comment), do_poller() (~lines 342-395 incl. divider comment + extensive comment block about client_activity polling), do_start_poller() (~lines 396-405 incl. comment). The @session-history-poller-pid option is referenced inside do_poller (lines ~369, ~393) and do_start_poller (line ~401) — these references disappear with the functions.
2. INPUT: The file scripts/session_history.sh in its current state, with the three functions present and the rest of the engine (do_hook, do_dwell, etc.) already PRD-compliant.
3. LOGIC: Delete the entire blocks for do_activity(), do_poller(), and do_start_poller() including their '# ---' divider comment headers and trailing blank lines. After deletion, run 'grep -n activity scripts/session_history.sh' and 'grep -n poller scripts/session_history.sh' to verify the ONLY remaining references are: (a) the case-dispatch branches (handled in S2) and (b) the do_init poller-start call (handled in T2). Do NOT modify do_hook, do_dwell, or any other function — they are already compliant.
4. OUTPUT: scripts/session_history.sh with do_activity/do_poller/do_start_poller removed. The engine no longer contains any client_activity polling code.
5. DOCS: none — the header comment rewrite is handled in P1.M1.T4 (Mode A, separate task). This subtask is pure code deletion.

subtasks.title: Remove activity/poller case-dispatch branches and update Usage string

CONTRACT DEFINITION:

The current case dispatch (bottom of scripts/session_history.sh, ~lines 635-650) has two extra branches: 'activity)  lock; load_alive; do_activity "$to"; unlock ;;' (~line 639) and 'poller)    do_poller ;;' (~line 640). tasks.title: Clean do_init() — Remove Poller Bootstrap & Pipe-Pane Legacy
tasks.description: Strip do_init of the pipe-pane legacy cleanup block and the do_start_poller() call so it matches PRD §17 ('Seed initial state if empty'). Add a one-shot stale-poller migration guard so upgrading users don't get orphaned poller processes.

subtasks.title: Remove pipe-pane legacy cleanup and poller start; add stale-poller migration guard
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/gap_analysis.md GAP 4b and GAP 7. do_init() (~lines 577-607) has three blocks after the seed logic: (1) seed logic (~lines 578-594) — COMPLIANT, KEEP UNTOUCHED; (2) pipe-pane legacy cleanup (~lines 595-601): reads @session-history-piped-pane, closes that pane's pipe via 'tmux pipe-pane -t ...', clears the option — DELETE (PRD §12 rejects pipe-pane plumbing; @session-history-piped-pane is not in PRD §3); (3) poller start (~lines 602-606): comment block + 'do_start_poller' call — DELETE (do_start_poller was removed in T1.S1; calling it would be a runtime error). CRITICAL MIGRATION ISSUE: after removing do_start_poller, a previously-started poller process (tracked in @session-history-poller-pid from a prior version) will keep running indefinitely because the reload no longer kills it. This must be handled.
2. INPUT: scripts/session_history.sh after T1.S1 has removed do_start_poller/do_poller/do_activity function bodies. do_init currently calls do_start_poller (which no longer exists).
3. LOGIC: (a) Delete the pipe-pane legacy cleanup block entirely (~lines 595-601, including the comment '# Legacy cleanup: ...'). (b) Replace the poller-start block (~lines 602-606) with a one-shot migration guard that runs BEFORE the existing save/return: read the old @session-history-poller-pid option value; if non-empty, attempt to kill that PID ('kill "$old_pid" 2>/dev/null'), then clear the option ('S "$(H poller-pid)" ""'). This ensures a user reloading after upgrade has their stale poller cleaned up on the first init. After this guard, do_init should be: seed-if-empty logic (unchanged) + one-shot stale-poller guard. Do NOT add any new background process starts. The guard is self-cleaning — once @session-history-poller-pid is cleared, subsequent inits skip it.
4. OUTPUT: do_init() matches PRD §17: 'Seed initial state if empty (current/attached session).' plus a defensive one-shot stale-poller migration guard. No new background processes are started.
5. DOCS: none — do_init is an internal subcommand; no user-facing surface change.

tasks.title: Update Dwell Default to 30000 ms
tasks.description: Change the dwell_ms() fallback default from 10000 to 30000 to match PRD §15. This is the coupled compensating change: once focused-activity detection is removed, dwell becomes the only silent-presence signal, so its threshold must be long enough (30 s) to avoid spurious promotion of sessions merely browsed past.

tasks.description: Rewrite the header comment block (lines 1-108) of scripts/session_history.sh to remove all references to focused-activity / client_activity polling and reflect the PRD §6 selection+dwell-only relevance model and the PRD §13 concurrency model where dwell is the only async path.

subtasks.title: Rewrite 'WHAT MAKES A SESSION RELEVANT' comment section
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/gap_analysis.md GAP 6a. The engine header (~lines 42-66) currently has a 'WHAT MAKES A SESSION RELEVANT?' bullet list that describes 'focused activity (the PRIMARY signal)' as the first and most important promotion cause, with detailed multi-paragraph text about client_activity timestamp polling, and dwell described only as 'the SILENT-PRESENCE fallback'. PRD §6 states authoritatively: a session is promoted by exactly two causes — (1) direct selection (any NAVIGATION or TOGGLE), (2) dwell (reaching by WALK and staying > dwell-ms). 'Walking never promotes.' PRD §12 explains why there is no output-activity signal.
2. INPUT: scripts/session_history.sh after T1.S1 (functions removed) and T3.S1 (dwell default changed). The header comment at ~lines 42-66 describes the OLD three-cause model.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite the 'WHAT MAKES A SESSION RELEVANT?' bullet list to match PRD §6 exactly: (1) direct selection — any NAVIGATION (pick/sessionx/manual switch) or TOGGLE promotes the session you land on to #1 immediately; (2) dwell — if you reach a session by a WALK (back/forward) and stay longer than @session-history-dwell-ms (default 30000 ms), it becomes #1. Remove ALL text about client_activity, polling, typing/output detection, alert-activity, pipe-pane, and the 'focused activity (the PRIMARY signal)' framing. State explicitly: 'Walking (back/forward) through a session does NOT promote it by itself.' Update any '(default 10000 ms)' references to '(default 30000 ms)'. The comment should mirror PRD §6's wording.
4. OUTPUT: The header's relevance-model section accurately describes the PRD §6 two-cause model with no activity-detection references.
5. DOCS: This IS the doc update (Mode A — inline documentation on the engine file). No separate docs subtask needed for this comment block.

subtasks.title: Rewrite CONCURRENCY comment section to remove activity/poller references
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/gap_analysis.md GAP 6c and GAP 6d. The CONCURRENCY comment block (~lines 89-104) currently names 'activity' as 'the second async path' alongside dwell, references do_poller/do_activity, describes the poller firing '~0.5 s', and calls it 'the only resident process for activity'. PRD §13 describes the concurrency model with dwell as the only async relevance path (there is no activity path). PRD §8 §10 explain why dwell touches only the relevance list. Also at ~line 124, the text 'keypresses are ~150 ms apart and the poller fires only every ~0.5 s' must have the poller clause removed.
2. INPUT: scripts/session_history.sh after T1.S1 (functions removed). The CONCURRENCY comment block still references the removed do_poller/do_activity.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite the CONCURRENCY section to match PRD §13: (a) keep the core flock serialization explanation (async hooks, prune+hook concurrency, flock on a stable file); (b) replace 'The TWO further async paths (dwell, activity)' with 'The ONE async path (dwell)' — dwell touches ONLY @session-history-tlist AND takes the lock; (c) remove all sentences about do_poller, do_activity, client_activity, the poller, '~0.5 s', 'the only resident process', and 'focused-activity detection'; (d) at ~line 124, remove 'and the poller fires only every ~0.5 s' from the contention note, keeping 'keypresses are ~150 ms apart, so contention is imperceptible'. The rewritten comment should mirror PRD §13's structure.
4. OUTPUT: The CONCURRENCY header comment accurately describes the PRD §13 model with dwell as the sole async path and no activity/poller references.
5. DOCS: This IS the doc update (Mode A — inline documentation on the engine file). No separate docs subtask needed for this comment block.

subtasks.title: Rewrite promotion model — remove activity bullet, keep selection + dwell
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/doc_impact.md §1b and §3. The README 'How it works' section (~lines 106-128) currently has a three-bullet promotion list where the FIRST bullet is 'type, switch panes/windows, or run any tmux command in it while viewing it — this is the primary signal' with extensive client_activity explanation. PRD §6 lists exactly TWO causes: (1) direct selection, (2) dwell. The 'But the instant you produce output in a walked-to session, activity promotes it immediately' paragraph (~lines 126-127) is false in the target state.
2. INPUT: README.md in its current state. The engine has already been refactored (P1.M1 done) so the code reflects selection+dwell-only.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite the 'A session becomes relevant' bullet list to exactly two bullets matching PRD §6: (1) 'select it directly' — via toggle, pick, tmux-sessionx, or a manual switch-client; (2) 'dwell on it' — reach it by walking (back/forward) and stay longer than @session-history-dwell-ms (default 30 s). Delete the entire 'type, switch panes/windows...' bullet, the client_activity explanation, the monitor-activity parenthetical, and the 'produce output... activity promotes immediately' paragraph. Rewrite the 'Walking through a session does not make it relevant' paragraph to explain that if you walk from A to B and toggle, you flip back to A (not the adjacent session), and if you stay on B long enough, dwell promotes it.
4. OUTPUT: README 'How it works' promotion model describes exactly two causes (selection + dwell) matching PRD §6, with no activity/typing/output references.
5. DOCS: This IS the doc update (Mode A — README section directly touched by the relevance-model change).

subtasks.title: Remove 'How activity detection works' subsection and rewrite async-paths paragraph
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/001_ca41c05f3ead/architecture/doc_impact.md §1c, §1d, §5, and §6. The README has a bolded '**How activity detection works.**' subsection (~lines 130-140) that describes the client_activity timestamp, the background poller (~0.5-1 s), and 'no per-pane pipes / one resident process'. PRD §12 explicitly says there is no output-activity signal. The async-paths paragraph (~lines 142-148) says 'The dwell timer is one asynchronous path; focused-activity detection is the other' and 'activity promotes it instead' — both false in the target state. PRD §8 describes dwell as the sole async path touching only the relevance list.
2. INPUT: README.md after S1 has rewritten the promotion model. The 'How activity detection works' subsection and the two-async-paths paragraph are still present.
3. LOGIC: (a) DELETE the entire '**How activity detection works.**' subsection (~lines 130-140). (b) Rewrite the async-paths paragraph (~lines 142-148) to state: 'The dwell timer is the only asynchronous path, and it touches only the relevance list (never the timeline), so a rare lost update only nudges relevance and self-heals on the next switch. When you walk onto a session, a background timer is armed; if you are still on that session when it fires, the session is promoted. The timer self-cancels if you have moved on, so stale timers are harmless.' Optionally add one sentence: 'Relevance intentionally comes from selection and dwell only: there is no robust tmux primitive for focused-session output detection without a resident process per pane.' Remove all 'focused-activity detection is the other', 'activity promotes it instead', 'one resident process' text. Note: with toggle unbound there are zero resident processes; with it bound the only background work is short-lived dwell timers.
4. OUTPUT: README has no 'How activity detection works' subsection. The async-paths paragraph describes dwell as the sole async path matching PRD §8/§13.
5. DOCS: This IS the doc update (Mode A — README section directly touched by the activity-removal change).
